messages:
customer_acme_ops: Hey, prod surge hitting us right now. Requests are queueing and were seeing 429s. Its been ~6m and the Dedicated pool didnt scale up. Were on a customer call, can someone escalate?

sarah_support: Sorry to hear that — were looking. Can you paste the request IDs or account id? Ill open an incident. :rotating_light:

autoscaler-bot: Alert: scale_up_failed for customer:acme - reason=min_replicas_bound, pending_pods=4, last_scale_attempt=2024-11-09T14:02:10Z
devon_oncall: I pulled the cluster view. Several pods stuck in Pending with reason=ImagePullBackOff and some Pending due to scheduling (InsufficientCPU) but actual node resource shows capacity free. Weird.
miguel_infra: AWS control-plane showing slower ENI attach times in us-west2 (avg 38s -> 90s) starting 14:00 UTC, plus a couple ECR throttles from the region. Could explain pod start lag.
lisa_engineer: Repro suggestion: from a test namespace run a rapid burst of requests and tail the warm-pool logs. Useful commands:```kubectl get pods -n redwood-serving -o wide``` ```kubectl describe pod <pending-pod>``` ```curl -v https://api.redwood.internal/v1/health --header 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'```
customer_acme_ops: Were seeing 503s from the gateway and 429s at the API layer. One sample request id: rq_01G4XYZ.
sarah_support: Thanks. Ive created INC-2024-1189 and added logs + request id. Tagging @devon_oncall and @lisa_engineer for triage.
devon_oncall: Quick triage notes: autoscaler attempted scale at 14:02:10, launched 4 pods, kubelet logs show image pull timeouts (context deadline exceeded) and the warmup hook (init-container) takes ~45s once pulled. Because the scheduler delays node attach the readiness probe never fires -> autoscaler sees pods unhealthy and aborts further scale iterations per backoff.
miguel_infra: Workaround options: 1) temporarily bump min_replicas from 1 to 3 for this customer to keep warm pods around, 2) enable reserved burst pool for 2 mins, 3) pre-pull images on node. Which do you want to try?
customer_acme_ops: Please bump min_replicas to 3 now. We can revert after traffic subsides.
lisa_engineer: Pushing config change to infra-config: set dedicated.minReplicas=3 for account:acme. Will monitor. Command snippet:```redwoodctl set-account-config --account acme --key dedicated.minReplicas --value 3```
sarah_support: change applied, autoscaler shows target min now 3. Noted in INC-2024-1189.
autoscaler-bot: Info: config_update detected for account:acme by lisa_engineer at 2024-11-09T14:08:33Z - new_min_replicas=3
devon_oncall: After bump we see 2 warm pods already ready within 90s, queue length dropping. Still watching for imagepull backoffs to ensure new replica count sustains.
miguel_infra: Filed cloud vendor ticket about ENI latency and ECR pull rate; vendor ticket CLOUD-987654. ETA from vendor ~45m.
customer_acme_ops: Thanks. On call says latency improving. Please keep me posted and confirm revert plan.
sarah_support: Will follow up in INC-2024-1189 and revert min_replicas when bursts return to normal (<10% of baseline for 15m). Also adding runbook step: if Pending pods due to ImagePullBackOff during surge -> consider temporary minReplicas bump + pre-pull.
ops_incident_mgr: Assigning owner: devon_oncall. Next update in 10m or on any regression.
devon_oncall: Owner ack. Will post logs and the kubectl outputs to the incident. Key action items: 1) wait for vendor fix on ENI/ECR (miguel), 2) monitor request queue and error rate (sarah), 3) evaluate permanent warm pool increase if this pattern repeats (lisa).
customer_acme_ops: Appreciate the quick response. Please escalate to engineering if we see another spike tomorrow.
sarah_support: Thanks — closing the call note, keeping incident open until vendor confirms fixed. :white_check_mark:
